Pakruojis Jewish Cemetery 2

Jewish Cemetery · Šiauliai County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Historians dispute when Pakruojis's Jewish community began — some trace it to the 16th century, others only to the late 18th, when the land belonged to the von Ropp family — but by the late 19th century Jews made up 70 percent of the town, a majority later diminished by significant emigration, much of it to South Africa. Of the town's three prewar synagogues, only the 1801 summer synagogue survives; reconstructed in 2017, it is now the oldest wooden synagogue in Lithuania and houses the children's section of the public library. After German forces handed local administration to Lithuanian collaborators in June 1941, mass killings took place at Morkakalnis, five kilometers away, in two actions in late July and early August — though a memorial plaque at the site gives a somewhat different date, an inconsistency worth noting rather than resolving. This, the newer of Pakruojis's cemeteries, lost its original wall during the Nazi occupation; today about 50 gravestones survive, roughly 30 inside a later wooden fence and 20 outside it, and a 1994 memorial stone was built from recovered tombstone fragments.
